newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle not well tested - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle not well tested - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle activity was extremely slow, with not enough traded to establish a solid market, feedlot sources said.

About 100 steers in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area that will likely grade select and choice sold at $62.00 per cwt, unchanged from last week's top price. An estimated 100 heifers also traded in the Panhandle, but at $64.00 delivered to the plant, they said.
There were no reported sales in Kansas.
Packer bids were at $62.00, with most cattle owners asking $64.00 to $65.00, with a few at $66.00, the sources said.
Strong CME live cattle futures and outlooks for higher beef prices contributed to the firm stance among owners to hold out for higher fed cattle prices, cattle feeders said.
Fed prices also were expected to be underpinned this week amid perceptions that feedlots were current and could wait for higher packer bids, they said.

Cattle weight gains were slipping a little from extreme heat during the day, but cooler temperatures and lower humidity in the evening were helping cattle cope with the heat, especially at Panhandle and Kansas feedlots, feeders said. Nebraska fed cattle gains also were not bad, they said.
